Theme

Body, health & movement

features noun

of the face

also facial features, lineaments, a feature of the face

classical

Liv. 21.4.2: habitum ōris līneāmentaque intuērī
Cic. Div. 1.23: līneāmenta ōris (Lewis & Short)

līneāmenta, līneāmentōrum n. pl.

noun, second declension, plural · Declension on Wiktionary

the features of the face; the lines of a face or a body

Of the face, ōris līneāmenta; of the whole body, corporis (Liv. 26.41, Lewis & Short). The singular līneāmentum is a drawn line.

Other words

  • ōs, ōris n. — the face, the features; also the mouth

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 5.16.9: ōs vultumque referēbat · Declension on Wiktionary

    With vultus, the expression (see face), it gives a person’s looks: ōs vultumque referre, to have someone’s face and features.

Examples

  • Hamilcarem juvenem redditum sibi veterēs mīlitēs crēdere, eundem vigōrem in vultū vimque in oculīs, habitum ōris līneāmentaque intuērī

    the old soldiers thought Hamilcar had been given back to them young: they saw the same vigour in his face, the same force in his eyes, the same expression and featuresLiv. 21.4.2

  • quae nōn minus mōrēs ejus quam ōs vultumque referēbat, tōtumque patrem mīrā similitūdine exscrīpserat

    she had his character no less than his face and features, and was the very copy of her fatherPlin. Ep. 5.16.9

See also face, feature.
